### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED (literal, a string literal in INDEX_NOT_PROVEN_CODE))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via admitSources (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), searchByKey (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), organizationIds (symbol, a field of interface AdmittedSource), KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED (literal, a string literal in INDEX_NOT_PROVEN_CODE))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb3f8b9538d167460d3a67c5201a1e6315e936e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `44ca5c6e76e88d05c18177d1d66b40e9c15a241f` — the merge of head `8979fd3768adaf6d934bb7813a21826249514800` into base `cb3f8b9538d167460d3a67c5201a1e6315e936e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 44ca5c6e76e88d05c18177d1d66b40e9c15a241f && git checkout 44ca5c6e76e88d05c18177d1d66b40e9c15a241f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cb3f8b9538d167460d3a67c5201a1e6315e936e2 8979fd3768adaf6d934bb7813a21826249514800 && git checkout -B drift-repro cb3f8b9538d167460d3a67c5201a1e6315e936e2 && git merge --no-ff 8979fd3768adaf6d934bb7813a21826249514800

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb3f8b9538d167460d3a67c5201a1e6315e936e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cb3f8b9538d167460d3a67c5201a1e6315e936e2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `458d4d9cbce1424435d0960d533afea81c425ccd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-source-admission.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-source-admission.test.ts + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-index-fingerprint.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/pgvector-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/turso-adapter.ts (cited code, read only); the changeset and content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx read sentence by sentence as the caller asked

Inputs: card #37467 (body, triage 7185274073, first touch 7192256688, claim 7217130727, dev report 7221149374), PR #37963 (body, file list, net diff against main), the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run. One commit outside the shallow clone (9981f27d96, #37337) was fetched and read to settle the history question.

Verdict in one line: the arm is removed correctly and the predicate is exact, but the proof the removal rests on has two paths on which an index reports the current fingerprint and recipe hash while still holding a document with a `title` value, so this head is not safe to land as a field-gate change.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set at search, non-system caller, source where `mayServeEarlierRuleTitle` is true: was "searched when the caller may query `title` and every other served field"; is "searched when the caller may query every served field AND `indexStatus` reports the current fingerprint and recipe hash". Narrower for callers who may query `title` (refused 409 until proven), wider for callers who may not (served once proven). Named right in the Clause-② line, with the exceptions in S2.
- Accept-set at search, every other source: unchanged. `servedFieldsOf` loses only the `title` add, and for a source outside the predicate that add was either absent (no `title` declared), removed again by the withheld set, or already present (display field is `title`, or the source lists it). Right.
- Accept-set at save (`admitAuthoredSource`, ADR-0161 K4 guard two): an author who may not query a declared `title` the source does not index is now admitted. Wider; the display field, each `content` and `metadataFields` member and the `where` fields are still asked. Right, and it is the only widening at the save door.
- Refusal surface: `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` / 409 gains a second cause emitted by `@objectstack/service-knowledge` itself. The package already holds the code in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (:1674), so no ledger move is owed. Right.
- Public exports: `mayServeEarlierRuleTitle` is exported from the module but not from `src/index.ts`; no package surface is added. `servedFieldsOf` has no reader outside the module. Right.
- System context: `admitSources` returns before any `proveIndex` is set when `ctx.isSystem`, so no `indexStatus` read and no refusal. A caller with no context, or a service with no engine, is still searched nothing. Right.
- Check-runs on the head: Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1 to 10 of 10, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, the Type Check lanes, Live E2E UI and Test UI all read success; the UI lanes and the Dogfood shards read skipped, as the dev report says.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/service-knowledge': patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: right under AGENTS.md ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). No key, accepted value or metadata type moves; the save door admits more authors, which is a permission answer and not a change to what a `knowledge_source` may say.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is one of the four readable spellings (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: a diff that widens one surface and narrows another) and both halves are real here. The line is present, line-initial, in the PR body and the changeset. The claim on the card said `Clause-②: no`; the dev raised it, which is the correct direction.
- The `!` in the title and the BREAKING banner agree with the arm.
- ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the reason sentence is true (nothing authored or stored is rewritten), and the gate read it green. The second BREAKING bullet does tell an adapter author to add two contract members; that is new code on an optional interface, not a rewrite of anything `objectstack migrate meta` reaches, so the category holds. See N4.
- The content of the Clause-② line and the BREAKING bullets is not accurate as written: S2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: "none"; this record disagrees (M1, S1).
- Out-of-scope note 1 (one `indexStatus` read per qualifying source per search, uncached): accepted. Caching would be wrong, since another node may rebuild or drop the index; the read is paid only where the predicate is true.
- Out-of-scope note 2 (the package suite, the admission file, tsc and the seven ablations ran outside the verify lock at --maxWorkers=2): for the seat. The CI lanes on the head ran the same suite and read success, so the test verdict does not rest on the unlocked runs; the ablation counts do, and nothing in CI repeats them. The dogfood battery ran under the lock.
- Premise correction (`:178` stays, only `:278` was the arm): correct. See ④ (d).
- The card was triaged as "security behaviour unchanged, clean-up, p3". The PR that came out is a declared BREAKING narrowing of a field-level read gate. Whether the first-touch ruling covers that is the seat's to answer, not this record's.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The added read is one adapter call per qualifying source.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — a complete walk that purges nothing still records the recipe hash, so "current hash" does not prove "no earlier-rule document", and `unprovenIndex` accepts it.
- Where: `walkObjectSource`, `knowledge-service.ts:945` on the head: `if (listed === undefined || cap !== undefined || (source.refresh?.onRecordChange ?? true) === false) return build ? this.completeBuild(...) : done;`. With `build` true this is reached in two declared configurations, and in both `completeBuild` records `ctx.index` with no purge having run: (1) an adapter with `indexStatus` and `completeBuild` but no `listDocuments` (`listAdapterDocuments` answers `{ ok: false }` with no reason, so `listingNote` is unset and the walk completes); (2) a source with `refresh.onRecordChange: false` on any adapter. The same two conditions stood at 9981f27d96 (:687 there), so every `rh1` hash ever recorded is subject to them.
- What stays behind: a document the walk did not see, that is, one whose row no longer matches the source's `where`. Such documents exist by design: a predicate write (`multi: true`) publishes a count and is not synced (plugin jsdoc, `enableEventSync`), a rolled-back write leaves one, and an opted-out source is never synced at all. If that document was assembled before #37301 its `title` is the value of the field named `title`.
- How it reaches the caller: chunk granularity is the default, and `applyPermissionFilter` (:2586) with `liveTitles` false asks only whether the caller can read the row by id. It does not re-ask `where` and does not compare `docHash`; that check lives only in `answerByRecord`. So a row that left `where` but is still readable passes, and the hit carries the stored title. The gate no longer asks about `title`, the proof reads "current", and a caller who may not query `title` is served its value. On main the arm refuses this caller.
- Reach: the three built-in adapters all implement `listDocuments`, and none of them can hold an earlier-rule document in a searched index anyway (memory is rebuilt by the running code; pgvector was born in #37337; Turso's generation tables postdate #37337 and its earlier-release table is refused, never searched, then dropped at `completeBuild`). So the arm's whole protective value is for a persistent adapter outside this repo, and that is exactly the population path (1) reaches. The changeset's own second fix ("implement `indexStatus` and `completeBuild` on the adapter, then rebuild") walks such an adapter into path (1) if it has no `listDocuments`.
- The claim this falsifies, as written in the module jsdoc, the changeset and the PR body: "a complete build rewrites each document whose title changed and purges the rest". The first half holds; the second holds only when the adapter lists and the source is synced. (A third, much narrower exception: `purgeDocuments` keeps a candidate whose row a re-read finds, and counts foreign ids as kept; the first needs a row to leave and re-enter `where` around the walk with no synced event, the second is not a document this service assembled. Named for completeness, not graded.)
- A fix that keeps the head's shape: fail closed at the proof. `unprovenIndex` already has the adapter and the source; treat a source as unproven when the adapter has no `listDocuments` or the source has `refresh.onRecordChange: false`, with its own operator sentence, and pin both. That makes those sources permanently refused for non-system callers, which is a further narrowing the changeset must then state. The alternative is to make the default-granularity filter drop a hit whose row no longer matches `where` for a `proveIndex` source. Which of the two is the dev's and the seat's call; the head as it stands is neither.

S1 (should-fix) — the recipe hash names what the last complete build walked under, not what later writes were made under, so a write between builds under another title field survives a return to the recorded recipe.
- Where: `writeSynced` (:2174) and `repairStale` write through `recordToDocument` with the schema as it reads at that moment, into the active generation; no adapter compares or records the recipe hash on `upsert`. An object definition changing at runtime starts no rebuild (`buildReloadedSource` is called only for a `knowledge_source` item, `knowledge-source-loader.ts:227`); the next boot pass is what would notice.
- Path: display field `name`, index built, hash R recorded. The object's `nameField` is set to `title`; records touched in that window are synced with `title` values as their document title. `nameField` is set back to `name` before any boot. `planIndex` computes R again, `indexStatus` still reports R, the source reads proven, and those documents are served at chunk granularity to a caller who may not query `title`. On main the arm refuses that caller. The same shape is reachable by a node still running pre-#37301 code beside an upgraded one during a rolling deploy.
- This is far narrower than M1 and may be accepted rather than closed, but it is the "event-sync write between builds" case and the proof text claims more than it delivers. Either close it or say it: a sentence in the module jsdoc and in `knowledge.mdx` that the proof covers what the last complete build walked, plus a follow-up card for chunk-level freshness, would be an honest floor. The seat should rule which.

S2 (should-fix) — the changeset's first BREAKING bullet and its fix are false for two declared configurations, and the Clause-② line omits them.
- "The boot's build pass builds a source whose index records no recipe hash or another one ... Fix: none is owed for a built-in adapter (memory, pgvector, Turso)". `buildIfDue` (:1384) returns before reading anything for a source with `refresh.onRecordChange: false`, at boot and on reload; and `KnowledgeServicePluginOptions.buildAtBoot: false` turns the whole pass off (plugin :565, and `buildOnReload` at :779). In both, on a built-in adapter, a qualifying source stays refused for every non-system caller until an operator runs `os knowledge rebuild`; on the memory adapter that repeats at every restart. For an opted-out source the rebuild is also the service writing an index the source declares an external indexer owns, and that indexer never calls `completeBuild`, so the refusal is in practice standing.
- These are prose faces, so the fix does not move code: name both configurations in the bullet, give `os knowledge rebuild` as the owed fix for them, and carry the same two into the Clause-② line's "until a complete build of the source has completed" and into the `knowledge.mdx` paragraph. If M1 is closed by failing closed, this text changes again with it.

S3 (should-fix) — the refusal's message and the operator line promise a rebuild will end a refusal that, on two adapter shapes, no rebuild can end.
- Caller-facing `message` (`planSearches`): "needs a rebuild ... It answers again once a complete rebuild of the source has completed." Operator `warn` line: ends "... once a complete build under the current recipe has completed (os knowledge rebuild)." Both are emitted unchanged when the reason is "the adapter reports no index status" (rebuilding changes nothing), and when the adapter has `indexStatus` but no `completeBuild`, where `unprovenIndex` says "the index records no recipe hash: no complete build of it has completed" although any number of complete walks may have run. `readIndexStateOf` (:1115 to :1124) already tells these two apart and says "nothing is rebuilt automatically"; the search-time text should say as much, so an operator does not loop on rebuilds. The permanence itself is correct and fails closed; only its statement is wrong.

Answers to the points asked, where not already above.

(a) The proof, step by step.
- Recorded only by post-#37301 code: holds. GitHub compare of 039b2884d4 against 9981f27d96 reads ahead 34, behind 0, so #37301 is an ancestor of #37337. At 9981f27d96 `documentTitle` already reads `record[documentTitleField(schema)]`, and `knowledge-index-fingerprint.ts` is added by that commit. `TITLE_RULE_VERSION` has been 1 since, and the hash body carries the resolved title field name, so a changed display field changes the hash.
- Recorded only at completion: holds for all three built-in adapters. memory `completeBuild` (:135), pgvector `completeBuild` and Turso `completeBuild` (:640) are the only writers of the recipe hash; `beginBuild` and `upsert` write none. `indexStatus` in each reports the ACTIVE generation's values, which is the generation a search reads.
- Partial build (`limit`), `dryRun`: `build` is false, no `beginBuild`, no `completeBuild`. Holds.
- A build that did not complete: every early return (fence stop, failed read, failed upsert, failed listing, purge failure, lease lost before completion) returns without `completeBuild`; a `completeBuild` that throws leaves the adapter's record as it was. Holds. During a rebuild inside the same generation the old hash is reported until completion, so the source stays refused throughout.
- `docHash` covers the title (`computeDocHash`: content, title, metadata, organization), and a listed hash that is absent or different is rewritten. Holds.
- "Purges every document it did not walk": does not hold. M1.
- Event-sync and `repairStale` writes between builds: made by current code under the recipe as it reads then; not tracked against the recorded hash. S1.
- Another adapter's `completeBuild` recording the hash without purging: this is M1 path (1).
- Per search, non-system only: yes. `proveIndex` is set in `admitSources` after the system return; `planSearches` runs once per `searchByKey` and reads `indexStatus` with no cache. The refill round reuses the proven list without a second read, which is sound: the only way an index moves between rounds is toward a newer build, and an adapter that switched generations refuses the refill itself.
- Search never starts a build: by construction. `planSearches` calls `planIndex` (settings and schema reads) and `adapter.indexStatus`, nothing else; the three built-in `indexStatus` bodies read generation rows and write nothing.

(b) `mayServeEarlierRuleTitle` is exact. On main the arm added `title` when the fields cannot be enumerated or declare `title`, then the withheld set removed it; it changed the answer only when `title` was not already served. The predicate is that condition term for term: not declared returns false, withheld returns false, already served (display field is `title`, no definition so the title field is `title`, or listed in `content` or `metadataFields`) returns false. No false negative found. False positives (fields not enumerable, no display field resolved, a deployment with no `security` service where every caller may query `title`) cost one read or a refusal, never a leak. The schema it reads (`objectAdmission.schema`, from `engine.getSchema`) is the one `planIndex` hashes (`schemaFor`, the same call).

(c) Permanent refusal: correct in code, fails closed (no `indexStatus`, or one that throws, or no `completeBuild` so no hash is ever recorded). Stated correctly in the changeset's second bullet and Clause-② line; stated incompletely in `knowledge.mdx` (N3) and wrongly in the runtime text (S3).

(d) `documentTitleField` answering `title` for an object with no definition (main :178) is the current assembly rule: `recordToDocument` reads `title` there too and the recipe hash names it. It stays, rightly. Only the `served.add('title')` at main :278 was the arm. The save-side widening is right: a save is judged on what the source will index under the current rule, and no index of a source being saved needs the arm. Nothing else widens at the save door.

(e) Every other arm unchanged: the diff to `servedFieldsOf` removes the `declared` read and the one `add`; `selectingFieldsOf`, `admitSourceFields`, `admitObject`, the withheld set and `applyPermissionFilter` are untouched. The three proven-index reverse pins hold the display field, a `content` field and a `metadataFields` field.

(f) Changeset and docs, beyond S2.
- Summary line and the closing paragraph: accurate apart from "and purges the rest" (M1).
- Clause-② line: the predicate, the code, the whole-refusal case, the permanence and the save widening are each stated correctly. It says "the object's display field is another field"; the predicate is also true when no display field resolves or the fields cannot be enumerated. N3.
- `knowledge.mdx` 3.2 paragraph: correct on the proof and the code. "The boot's build pass or `os knowledge rebuild` builds it" is true as an either-or. The last sentence covers no `indexStatus` and omits no `completeBuild`. The field-rules bullet correctly drops "and a declared `title` field".
- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` :297 still gives one cause for the code. N2.

(g) Tests. The refusal is pinned five ways with code and status, for a caller who may and one who may not query `title`, with the adapter never searched. The proof path is pinned (served, `indexStatus` read once; refused, rebuilt, `current`, served). The system bypass is pinned inside each unproven case. The no-read case is pinned (`indexStatus` not called for three non-qualifying sources). The predicate table has seven rows covering each term. Not pinned: that a refused search starts no build (N1), and either M1 configuration (the stateful stub lists an empty index and no case completes a walk without a purge). The ablation counts are plausible against the cases but were measured outside the lock and are not re-run by any check-run; they are the dev's reading, not a gate verdict.

(h) Ordering against #37306. Three parts of this reasoning read `planSearches` as it stands and need a second look at the merge: the adapter whose `indexStatus` is read must be the adapter `searchRound` then searches, so both lookups must resolve through the same binding once `boundAdapterId` lands; the `!adapter` branch pushes the entry with no proof, which is safe only because `searchRound` refuses an unmounted adapter and never falls back to another; and the destructure that strips `proveIndex` must survive the hunk so the flag is neither lost before the check nor carried into `SearchTarget`. The whole-refusal test (`first.size === 0 and refused.length above 0`) also depends on `planSearches` filling the same `refused` array before the first round.

N1 (nit) — no case asserts that a refused search calls neither `beginBuild`, `upsert` nor `completeBuild`; one line in the stateful case before the rebuild would pin "search never starts a build".
N2 (nit) — `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` :297 says a search answering `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` "says the source is being rebuilt"; the code now has a second cause and the page does not name it.
N3 (nit) — the Clause-② line and the `knowledge.mdx` paragraph describe the qualifying source more narrowly than the predicate (they omit an object whose fields cannot be enumerated or that resolves no display field, and the doc omits the no-`completeBuild` adapter).
N4 (nit) — the ADR-0087 marker holds, but its reason could say in so many words that the adapter author's fix is new code on optional contract members and not a rewrite, since the body does carry a "Fix:" aimed at a consumer.
N5 (nit) — the reflowed field-rules bullet in `knowledge.mdx` leaves one over-long line.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK** at head `458d4d9cbce1424435d0960d533afea81c425ccd` (Fixes #37467). Full read · 2026-11-27T14:57Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** `l1-face --pr 37963`: one flag, dogfood owed. The dev report's battery is 490 of 493 files with 3 skipped, so that flag is met. Check-runs at 458d4d9c: 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed. `!` title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, so a contract review is owed.

**Contract review.** Record 7221441058 at this head is a FAIL, served at the contract tier (`verify-review-tier` PASS): M1, plus S1, S2 and S3. I adopt it. What holds: the predicate `mayServeEarlierRuleTitle` matches the old arm term for term, #37301 is an ancestor of #37337 so no recipe hash was ever recorded by code that wrote `title`, the system bypass and the no-build-on-search are by construction, and every other arm of the gate is unchanged.

**Owed before ACCEPT.**
1. **M1, the proof does not hold on two paths.** I confirmed the line: at `knowledge-service.ts:945` on this head, `walkObjectSource` calls `completeBuild` with no purge when the adapter has no `listDocuments` (`listed === undefined`) or the source has `refresh.onRecordChange: false`. The recipe hash is then recorded although documents the walk did not see, such as a row that left `where` through a predicate write, keep an earlier-rule title. At chunk granularity those hits reach a caller who may not query `title`. The record gives two shapes of fix. Pick one and pin it. The record's own lean is to fail closed in `unprovenIndex` for those two source shapes, which the changeset must then state as part of the narrowing.
2. **S1, writes between builds.** A display-field change and change-back at runtime leaves event-synced documents of the middle window under a hash that reads current. It is much narrower than M1.
